thread:
rebecca: Quick question from the all-hands Q&A: can we get a concise summary of the updated release rhythm and how it affects oncall?
noah: Short version: minor releases every 3 weeks, majors once a month. Oncall expectations mostly same but notify windows tightened.
tracy: What are the exact notification windows? ops needs to coordinate maintenance windows with sales.
evan: Ops asked for 24h pre-notify for planned canaries, a 2h pre-ramp reminder, and immediate alert on rollback. Add a slack ping + post to #incidents.
rebecca: Feature flags still mandatory for user-facing changes?
noah: Yes — all customer-facing changes behind a flag or go via a controlled canary for 24h. Infra-only patches that don't touch APIs are exempt.
tracy: Quality bar specifics? perf thresholds? regressions triggers?
ops: Checklist: unit + integration pass, staging smoke e2e green, perf check: p99 no worse than 15% over baseline, error rate <0.5% absolute. If exceeded, rollback.
oncall-bot: Reminder: add a "canary runbook" to the release ticket and tag @ops 24h prior.
rebecca: SLA questions: will hosted SLAs be adjusted because of the faster minor cadence? customers asking.
product: No SLA changes. We'll provide internal per-route SLO dashboards so PMs and AE can see risk ahead of renewals.
kelsey: Can we get a short one-page internal checklist (cadence, notif, rollback criteria) and a customer-facing blurb? happy to draft.
ohan: Typo — meant to say "noah" :facepalm:
oops: :thumbsup: docs + product to collaborate on two artifacts: internal checklist + customer blurb. We'll also add calendar blockers for major customer maintenance days.
rebecca: Thanks — if someone can drop the PR/notes in the handbook and tag oncall + sales that would be perfect.
